name: e2fsprogs
desc: Utilities for the ext2, ext3, and ext4 file systems
why: The ext2/3/4 filesystem toolkit; poking at debugfs and on-disk structures is a real door into file formats, but it is familiar plumbing.

brief.what_it_is: e2fsprogs is the set of userland utilities for the ext2, ext3, and ext4 Linux filesystems. The homepage describes it as the filesystem utilities for ext2, with support for ext3 and ext4. The executables listed include mke2fs and mkfs.ext2 for making filesystems, e2fsck and fsck for checking them, resize2fs for resizing, debugfs for interactive inspection, dumpe2fs for dumping superblock and group info, tune and label tools such as e2label, and helpers such as badblocks, blkid, chattr, lsattr, filefrag, e2image, e2undo, and uuidgen. It takes a block device or image file as input and acts on its on-disk structures.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it provides the filesystem utilities for use with the ext2 filesystem, and it is maintained by Theodore Ts'o. The README says new versions are released from time to time to fix bugs and make the utilities more robust.
brief.install_notes: The GitHub README says the INSTALL file has instructions for building and installing e2fsprogs, and that it includes provisions for building Red Hat RPMs and Debian dpkg packages. The homepage says the development sources are in a git repository at git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/fs/ext2/e2fsprogs.git. I did not fetch the INSTALL file, so the exact build steps and dependencies are unverified. No accounts, hardware, or runtime requirements were mentioned.
brief.standout: Nothing in the pages I read marks it as unusual. It is the long-standing reference userland for the ext family, and the executables list is broad. The scout note's suggestion that debugfs is a window into on-disk structures is plausible from the tool list but was not confirmed by the README.
brief.status: Unknown, leaning maintained. The homepage announces release 1.47.4 as available and urges all users to upgrade, and the GitHub README also says this is version 1.47.4. But the homepage footer reads 'Last modified: Wed Dec 22 19:13:31 EST 2010', which conflicts with a 1.47.4 announcement. I did not find a release date or last commit date, so I cannot confirm recency.
brief.caveats: The README is thin: it covers version, contact, and where to find the INSTALL file, and gives no usage examples. The homepage's last-modified date (2010) does not match its release announcement. No license was mentioned in what I read. Bug reports are directed to a personal email address. The homepage links were not exposed as URLs in the fetched text, so the release notes and tutorial links are unverified.
